Ker --lcore-mask / [dpdk] lcore_mask accepts nonzero hex with optional0x/0X and surrounding whitespace, preserves multi-bit selection, and rejects blank/zero/non-hex before library or worker setup. CLI overrides INI before mask validation. Competing EAL -c/-l/--lcores selections are rejected rather than silently rewritten; original DPDK validates CPU availability and hardware/build limits. Real net_tap TCP in both roles uses two allowed physical CPUs in the INI mask, then CLI override to one of them. Actual DPDK lcore_count/main_lcore and host sched_getcpu are checked, plus original Linux TCP open counters, bidirectional Ethernet traffic and zero outstanding buffers. This adapts parsing/core-selection scenarios; F-Stack nb_procs/proc_lcore memory layout, process-per-core behavior, process-id selection, secondary processes and OOM paths are not implemented or claimed. Existing raw EAL mapping works unchanged when mask is absent.

Actual ker-io-worker with original DPDK net_tap in a private user/network namespace, no mocked EAL or counters. Idle start followed by repeated real control-channel stop requests and EOF must emit exactly one successful DONE with zero packets/bytes/directional validation drops/retries/outstanding. A second real worker forwards three exact Ethernet frames of60/127/1514 bytes each direction between independent host AF_PACKET and the native packet channel; expected counts are3 packets/1701 bytes each way. Two malformed channel frame lengths increment only TX validation drops; aggregate dropped remains2. Channel framing and complete received bytes are checked. Both stops close the ethdev and report zero in-use mbufs. The test harness uses SIGSTOP/SIGCONT only as a scheduling barrier while it queues both control bytes and closes the pipe; worker shutdown is still driven by the real control channel and EOF. This adapts zero-init traffic and idempotent stop scenarios, without F-Stack ff_traffic_args/getter/stop ABI or Linux networking coverage claims. Byte counts exclude the12-byte channel header and FCS; TX counts PMD acceptance and RX counts successful channel delivery, once per frame rather than retry. Drops are adapter validation drops, not NIC hardware or shutdown-discard counters.

Seed original Linux RNG from32 actual host SYS_getrandom syscall (flags0) bytes after private kernel boot and before application sockets are exposed. Original Linux RNDADDENTROPY mixes the seed and credits256 bits, followed by RNDRESEEDCRNG to rekey immediately even when already initialized; a private rootfs random-device node is unlinked immediately after open, descriptors close, and seed storage is explicitly wiped on every return. Actual original-kernel getrandom(GRND_NONBLOCK) fills64 bytes with the pinned >=50 nonzero threshold and yields >=12 changes across16 words. A test-only syscall wrapper injects EIO/zero/EINTR, failure after a real short read, and caps real successful reads at7 bytes; a deterministic getrandom symbol shim confirms seeding bypasses interposition, while successful entropy always comes from the real host RNG, never test constants. Both retry and ordinary/reseed paths use real original Linux ioctl/getrandom; host seeding invokes SYS_getrandom directly. A real private-path collision propagates EEXIST and preserves marker contents. This is a Linux RNG scenario adaptation, not FreeBSD arc4random API or algorithm equivalence; output sanity tests are not a cryptographic-strength proof. No custom PRNG, deterministic fallback, GRND_INSECURE, upstream modification or host random-device write.

Boot original Linux and invoke the same private realtime synchronization adapter used by the production constructor. Reset only native realtime to an obsolete2000 epoch, synchronize from real host CLOCK_REALTIME, and require native seconds/nanoseconds to lie within host bracketing reads and exceed the pinned2020 threshold. Native realtime advances after a real sleep; native monotonic advancement tracks host monotonic across the epoch change. Test-only clock_gettime wrapping forwards all monotonic reads to the real host clock. Host realtime EIO propagates without setting native time; a successful host read with invalid nanoseconds reaches original Linux clock_settime and returns EINVAL without mutating the old epoch. Recovery and repeated synchronization succeed. No host clock is set, upstream kernel code changed, or FreeBSD cached-time/NULL-output API equivalence claimed.

Real host thread creation, identity and joining are verified, together with actual LKL pthread TLS isolation.
cases.remaining: F-Stack inherits the opaque FreeBSD pcurthread pointer; LKL does not expose that contract. Child pthread TLS is intentionally empty, so this is not equivalent context propagation.

cases.reason: Real LKL host threads receive distinct argument objects and preserve their values through join and synchronized concurrent work.
Real LKL threads complete work and join successfully; joined results are observed through owned argument storage.
cases.remaining: LKL takes a void start routine and thread_join has no result pointer. The F-Stack-specific assertion that a non-NULL routine return becomes NULL cannot be expressed through this callback API.

cases.reason: Fail the actual LKL thread-wrapper allocation: thread_create returns its zero failure sentinel, errno remains ENOMEM and the routine never runs; F-Stack uses -ff_ENOMEM instead.
F-Stack pthread wrapper propagates FreeBSD pcurthread/per-CPU TLS and injects ff_malloc failures; Ker/LKL has a different host-thread runtime.
